blocks.text: The hijama cups are most often placed on the person’s back. In the case of facial or cosmetic hijama, the cups are applied to your face.

sections.heading: Types of Cupping Therapy We Provide

blocks.text: Weprovide the following types of cupping therapy in our hijama centre in Rawalpindi.

It is the most common type of cupping. During dry cupping, our hijama experts put a special cup on your skin and then suck out the air inside it. The cup stays there for about 5 to 10 minutes. There’s no breaking of the skin.

During wet cupping, our professional puts a special cup on your skin and leaves it there for a little while to suck your skin up a bit. Then, tiny cuts are made on your skin and the cup is put back to pull out a little blood. The cup stays there for about 10-15 minutes.

sections.heading: What should I expect during a cupping treatment?

blocks.text: You will undergo the following during cupping therapy:

items: A special cup is placed on your skin.
You might feel a pulling sensation.
Your skin might get red and puffy.
The cup stays on for a few minutes.
You might feel sore or relaxed.
After removing the cup, your skin might be red with small circles.

blocks.text: Hijama has tremendous benefits for human health. Some of them are:

The suction created by the cups can enhance circulation, potentially aiding in muscle recovery and relaxation

Hijama, or cupping therapy increases circulation in the treated area by creating a vacuum effect. When a cup is placed on the skin, a vacuum is created, dilating the blood vessels and resulting in increased blood flow to the area. This helps relieve pain, muscle relaxation, tissue repair, and detoxification.
Cupping may help with skin conditions such as pimples, acne, skin allergies, etc., by increasing blood flow to the area.
The process of hijama relaxes the body's muscles and can induce relaxation and stress reduction.
Some people find it helpful in reducing inflammation associated with various conditions.
